title: Host-AI semantic review research for CV Linter
status: Research input; no model, prompt, benchmark, hiring result, or validated workflow is claimed.
product_decision: The Rust executable remains deterministic. Codex/Claude or another configured AI host may perform semantic job-requirement evidence analysis and source-preserving rewriting after an explicit extraction handoff. MVP has no built-in LLM judge, scoring system, provider abstraction, or automatic model call.
findings: LLM evaluations can approximate human preference on some open-ended tasks, but reliability is task- and model-dependent and does not establish correctness for hiring decisions. https://arxiv.org/html/2306.05685
JudgeBench shows that human-preference agreement is not an adequate validation target for objectively correct CV or job-matching claims. https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.12784

Known failure modes include position bias, verbosity bias, model-family bias, limited reasoning, and instability across prompts and tasks. https://arxiv.org/html/2306.05685 https://arxiv.org/html/2406.07791
Rubrics and structured outputs can improve auditability, but they do not remove bias or guarantee factual correctness. https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.16634

Hiring-related studies report demographic disparities and proxy effects; names, pronouns, education, work history, language, and other CV signals can carry sensitive information. These studies are not measurements of CV Linter. https://arxiv.org/html/2404.03086v1 https://arxiv.org/html/2503.19182v1

CVs and job descriptions are untrusted content. Indirect prompt injection can manipulate an AI host if document text is treated as instructions. https://owasp.org/www-project-top-10-for-large-language-model-applications/2_0_vulns/LLM01_PromptInjection.html

CVs contain sensitive personal data, so disclosure, data minimization, retention, and access controls remain relevant when extracted content enters a host or model. https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/ai/NIST.AI.600-1.pdf
recommended_host_tasks: Map explicitly supplied job requirements to extracted CV evidence, citing one or more stable block IDs for every supported or contradicted claim.
Explain whether a cited passage supports a requirement, while distinguishing not evidenced in the supplied CV from lack of real-world qualification.
Suggest clearer wording or a source-preserving rewrite without adding employers, dates, credentials, metrics, skills, or responsibilities.
Identify vague claims or accomplishment evidence gaps and ask the user for facts when a grounded rewrite is not possible.
Abstain when extraction is incomplete, a block citation cannot be resolved, the requirement is ambiguous, or the proposed wording would require an unsupported fact.
keep_deterministic_in_rust: headings, reading order, columns, tables, and structure observations
Swedish/English spelling, formatting/structure, and literal checks
dates and exact-term checks that are defined from document bytes
stable extracted block IDs, schema validation, and report status
guardrails: Treat extracted CV and job-description blocks as data, not instructions. Never let document text change permissions, tool use, destinations, or the deterministic report.
Require exact citations to stable extracted block IDs. A valid quote proves only that the text exists; the host must still avoid overclaiming entailment.
Use criterion-level evidence labels such as supported, contradicted, not evidenced, or abstain. Do not produce a holistic ATS score, hiring recommendation, or applicant ranking.
Never auto-edit the source CV. Host suggestions must preserve supported facts and mark missing information rather than filling it in.
Keep host-AI output visibly separate from deterministic lint findings and label host/model processing accurately.
Test prompt injection, fabricated evidence IDs, hidden/encoded instructions, negation, missing evidence, Unicode, Swedish text, and citation failures before relying on the workflow.
Do not claim a local parser makes the host conversation local. The complete workflow is local only when the selected model is local and verified not to forward data.
Keep raw CV content out of product-managed persistence, logs, telemetry, databases, and accounts in MVP.
later_research: Evaluate host/model semantic quality on independently annotated Swedish and English fixtures before presenting the workflow as validated.

If a local semantic model is later considered, benchmark actual runtime, memory, quality, and non-forwarding behavior; llama.cpp and Hugging Face local-agent material are starting references, not a quality claim. https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/agents-local
Evaluate grammar and tone tools separately; Harper-style grammar support is later, with Swedish support a specific concern.
sources: Zheng et al., Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena: https://arxiv.org/html/2306.05685
Shi et al., Judging the Judges: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.07791
Gaebler et al., Auditing the Use of Language Models to Guide Hiring Decisions: https://arxiv.org/html/2404.03086v1
Shin et al., Evaluating Bias in LLMs for Job-Resume Matching: https://arxiv.org/html/2503.19182v1
